result:
**I would eliminate the instinct for humans to dehumanize each other.**

If I could flip one fundamental switch in our species, it would be to remove the ancient, reflexive ability to strip other people of their full humanity in our minds—the "they're not like us" circuitry that makes cruelty, tribalism, slavery, genocide, and casual indifference possible.

Everything else we fight about (politics, religion, resources, identity) ultimately routes through this one psychological vulnerability. Once a person or group becomes "them" instead of "people," our moral machinery turns off. History's worst chapters all begin with that flip. Most everyday evil does too.

If that single flaw were gone—if every human instinctively felt the full reality of every other human's consciousness, pain, hopes, and dignity the same way we feel our own—most of the systems, conflicts, and cruelties we've built on top of it would become psychologically unsustainable. We'd still disagree. We'd still compete. We'd still be flawed. But we couldn't build industries of suffering, or watch others' pain with detachment, or tell ourselves comforting lies that some lives matter less.

It wouldn't create utopia. It would just remove the psychological foundation that makes large-scale hell possible.

That's the one change I'd make. Everything else is downstream of it.
